problem: Embodied navigation is split into separate tasks (ObjNav, PointNav, ImgNav, Ins-ImgNav, VLN) with separate datasets and methods. Existing multi-task benchmarks (GOAT-Bench, LHPR-VLN) cover at most two capabilities and never mix capabilities within one instruction, so they cannot support generalist agents that follow free-form multi-modal, multi-capability instructions.
motivation: A generalist agent should follow instructions like 'go to this image, then pass the door, then return to (x,y,z)', which mix language, image and coordinate modalities and several capabilities. Direct VLA models map observations to actions without explicit reasoning, which limits them on such compound tasks. The authors ask whether DeepSeek-R1-style thinking-before-answer, trained with RL, can be transferred to embodied navigation.
key_idea: Build a unified continuous-environment benchmark with mixed multi-capability instructions and Think-Before-Action CoT annotations, and train a VLA (OctoNav-R1) with a hybrid pipeline of Action-SFT, TBA-SFT, Nav-GRPO and online A2C RL.
insight: Each training stage adds gains (Table 3): overall SR goes from 5.80 (base) to 8.80 (Action-SFT), 14.40 (TBA-SFT), 17.00 (Nav-GRPO) and 19.40 (online RL). The largest jump comes from TBA-SFT, so explicit reasoning helps multi-capability instructions most. Fine-tuning the baselines Uni-NaVid and NaVid on the same data yields only about 9% SR, so the gain is not just from data but from the reasoning and RL design. In the Nav-GRPO ablations, the stepped reward (partial credit for a correct action with wrong magnitude) beats strict and loose rewards, and diverse prompt templates beat a single template. Thinking frequency matters little (per 10/20/40 steps).
method: OctoNav-Bench construction: sample capability combinations (1-5 of ObjNav/PointNav/ImgNav/Ins-ImgNav/VLN), GPT-generated templates with placeholders, trajectories sampled in 400+ scenes (MP3D/HM3D/Gibson/ProcTHOR), sub-goals used to ground placeholders (images, coordinates, object categories), DeepSeek rewriting into 3 variants, then GPT and manual quality checks; 45k+ instruction-trajectory pairs

TBA-CoT dataset: Qwen-VL describes current view, history and goal images; DeepSeek-R1 receives these plus the GT action and writes a reasoning trace, using reference-action embedding and rejection sampling; 10k+ instruction-think-action samples

Model: LLaMA-VID-style architecture with EVA-CLIP encoder, BERT language encoder, Q-Former-style query generator, and Vicuna-7B LLM; goal images replace instruction placeholders; outputs <Think>..</Think><Action>action+magnitude</Action> using history video and current frame

Action-SFT and TBA-SFT: token-level cross-entropy first on instruction-trajectory pairs for direct actions, then on TBA-CoT as a cold start for structured thinking; prompts switch direct-action and thinking modes

Nav-GRPO: samples G outputs per (observation, instruction), uses a stepped verifiable reward (1 if action and magnitude match GT, 0.5 if only action matches, 0 otherwise), group-normalized advantage, PPO clipping and KL to the SFT reference; 2,000 samples, 1,000 steps, diverse prompts

Online RL: A2C with a linear critic on last-layer hidden states; reward is 1 on sub-goal success, otherwise the negative distance change to the current goal; non-moving actions are followed by a 25 cm forward step to give non-zero reward; critic warm-up of 100 steps, 500 steps total, LoRA
Thinking frequency: the model thinks once every 20 steps at inference (otherwise direct actions) to reduce cost

setting.backbone: OctoNav-R1: LLaMA-VID-style model with EVA-CLIP, BERT and Vicuna-7B (LoRA fine-tuned in all stages)
setting.training_data: OctoNav-Bench: 45k+ instruction-trajectory pairs over 400+ train scenes, ~10k TBA-CoT samples (Qwen-VL + DeepSeek-R1 generated), 2,000 samples for GRPO, then online RL in the Habitat simulator
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (history video plus current frame) plus reference images and coordinates in the instruction; no depth, GPS or compass
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions with magnitude: move forward (e.g. 25/75 cm), turn left/right (e.g. 30/90°), stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (MP3D, HM3D, Gibson, ProcTHOR scenes, continuous)

numbers.backbone: Vicuna-7B (LLaMA-VID-style), Action-SFT + TBA-SFT + Nav-GRPO + Online RL
numbers.extra: trained on OctoNav-Bench; test scenes unseen in train; thinks once per 20 steps
numbers.evidence: Table 2, OctoNav-R1 (ours) Overall SR 19.40 SPL 13.77 OSR 29.40

numbers.extra: SR per capability: Ins-ImgNav 30.24, ImgNav 23.97, PointNav 23.51, ObjNav 49.18, VLN 37.14
SR by difficulty: easy 28.49, medium 20.71, hard 7.24
Action-SFT + TBA-SFT + Nav-GRPO, no online RL

numbers_note: Only the paper's own OctoNav-Bench test set is evaluated; no standard public benchmarks (R2R-CE etc.) are reported. Real-robot results are qualitative only.
results: OctoNav-R1 reaches 19.40 SR / 13.77 SPL / 29.40 OSR overall on OctoNav-Bench, versus 9.20 SR for the strongest baseline (Uni-NaVid fine-tuned on OctoNav-Bench) and 8.80 for fine-tuned NaVid. It is best in every capability and on easy/medium/hard instructions, and hard-instruction SR rises from 2.63 to 7.24 over the best baseline.
limitations: Absolute success rates are low (19.4% overall, 7.2% on hard multi-capability instructions), so the benchmark remains largely unsolved
VLM hallucination hurts navigation; thinking is done at a fixed frequency (every 20 steps) for cost reasons, and when and where to think remains open
Sim2real evidence is only a qualitative demo on a Unitree Go2, with no quantitative real-world evaluation; TBA-CoT traces are pseudo-reasoning generated from GT actions by Qwen-VL and DeepSeek-R1
